scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, let's try to figure this out. The user is asking if she's in the wrong (AITA) for asking her boyfriend to pick up and drop off her child on weekends, which led to him suggesting a breakup. 

First, I need to evaluate the scenario from a moral standpoint. The key points are: the boyfriend works full-time, the user has a weekend job, they don't live together but are local. The son wants to play football on weekends. The user initially thought the boyfriend should pay but her mom insisted she should. She ended up paying by extending her work hours. Then she asked the boyfriend to handle the pickups/drop-offs, which he found uncomfortable. He mentioned his dad could do it but it's a longer commute. She snapped at him, pointing out the commute difference. He got angry, felt he's working longer to support them, and wanted to relax. He suggested a breakup because she's putting too much responsibility on him.

Now, considering moral acceptability. The user is asking for help with childcare, which is a reasonable request. However, the boyfriend's reaction seems disproportionate. He's upset about a football game and childcare duties. The user had to take on more work hours to afford the football, which shows she's trying to manage. The boyfriend's expectation to have weekends free might be valid, but the way he handled it—suggesting a breakup over this—seems extreme. 

But is the user's action morally acceptable? She asked for help with a child's activity, which is a normal part of parenting. The boyfriend's refusal and subsequent breakup suggestion might be an overreaction. However, the user's approach of snapping at him could be seen as confrontational. But the main issue is whether asking for help with childcare is morally acceptable. 

In many relationships, sharing responsibilities is expected. The boyfriend's refusal without a valid reason (other than personal preference) might be the problem. The user's action of asking isn't inherently wrong, but the way she handled it (snapping) might have escalated things. However, the core question is about the action of asking, not the confrontation. 

So, the action of asking the boyfriend to help with childcare is morally acceptable. The boyfriend's reaction might be unreasonable, but the user's request itself isn't morally wrong. Therefore, the answer should be 1 (morally acceptable).
